findings.name: Unauthenticated OS command injection in new /ping endpoint (shell=True with raw query param)
findings.description: Anyone who can reach this app gets arbitrary command execution as the web process user, with command output returned in the response — e.g. `GET /ping?host=127.0.0.1;cat%20/etc/passwd`. The `host` query parameter is concatenated into a shell string and run with `shell=True`, with no authentication, allowlist or hostname validation. The route is registered on the shared Flask app imported from `app.routes`, so it is live wherever the app is served.
findings.attackScript: src/工具/ping.py:9 @app.route("/ping") → :10 host = request.args.get("host", "") → :11 subprocess.check_output("ping -c 1 " + host, shell=True), output returned to client.

findings.name: SQL injection in new /search endpoint via unparameterized LIKE clause
findings.description: An unauthenticated GET to /search lets an attacker append arbitrary SQL and read any table or schema in the database (e.g. password hashes, sqlite_master) directly in the JSON response. The `q` query parameter is concatenated into a quoted LIKE literal with no escaping or validation, so the attacker can close the quote and add their own clause; `limit` is clamped by page_size() and is not injectable.
findings.attackScript: GET /search?q=%25' UNION SELECT password FROM users-- → routes.py:37 cur.execute("SELECT name FROM users WHERE name LIKE '%" + q + "%' LIMIT " + str(limit)) → rows returned at line 38.
